questions.question: What is the expected major product when Acetone (CH3COCH3) is treated with Bromine (Br2) / Acetic acid?
questions.explanation: Treating Acetone (CH3COCH3) with Bromine (Br2) / Acetic acid yields Bromoacetone + HBr. Rationale: Enol intermediate attacks bromine; introduction of electron-withdrawing bromine slows subsequent enolization.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Acetophenone (PhCOCH3) into Sodium benzoate (PhCOONa) + Iodoform precipitate (CHI3)?
questions.explanation: To convert Acetophenone (PhCOCH3) into Sodium benzoate (PhCOONa) + Iodoform precipitate (CHI3), the appropriate reagent is Excess I2 / aqueous NaOH. Rationale: Exhaustive alpha-triiodination turns -CI3 into a leaving group, cleaved by hydroxide into yellow iodoform.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Propanoic acid (CH3CH2COOH) is treated with 1. Br2, PBr3; 2. H2O?
questions.explanation: Treating Propanoic acid (CH3CH2COOH) with 1. Br2, PBr3; 2. H2O yields 2-Bromopropanoic acid + HBr. Rationale: PBr3 converts acid to acid bromide; enol brominates at alpha-carbon, followed by water hydrolysis.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 2-Methylcyclohexanone into Lithium 6-methylcyclohex-1-en-1-olate (kinetic enolate)?

options.label: A
options.text: 1. NaOEt; 2. Benzyl bromide; 3. Aqueous H3O+, heat

questions.explanation: To convert 2-Methylcyclohexanone into Lithium 6-methylcyclohex-1-en-1-olate (kinetic enolate), the appropriate reagent is LDA in THF (-78°C). Rationale: Sterically hindered LDA deprotonates the less hindered, more accessible alpha-CH2 carbon at -78°C.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when 2-Methylcyclohexanone is treated with Sodium hydride (NaH) in THF (25°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating 2-Methylcyclohexanone with Sodium hydride (NaH) in THF (25°C) yields Sodium 2-methylcyclohex-1-en-1-olate (thermodynamic enolate). Rationale: Equilibrating conditions at room temperature favor the more substituted, more stable enolate double bond.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Lithium 6-methylcyclohex-1-en-1-olate into 2,6-Dimethylcyclohexanone?
questions.explanation: To convert Lithium 6-methylcyclohex-1-en-1-olate into 2,6-Dimethylcyclohexanone, the appropriate reagent is Iodomethane (CH3I). Rationale: The kinetic enolate nucleophile attacks methyl iodide via SN2, alkylating the less hindered alpha position.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1. NaOEt; 2. Benzyl bromide; 3. Aqueous H3O+, heat to yield 3-Phenylpropanoic acid as the major product?
questions.explanation: Diethyl malonate reacts with 1. NaOEt; 2. Benzyl bromide; 3. Aqueous H3O+, heat to yield 3-Phenylpropanoic acid. Rationale: Monoalkylation of diethyl malonate followed by acid hydrolysis of diester and thermal decarboxylation.

questions.topic: Malonic ester dialkylation to cyclic carboxylic acid
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Diethyl malonate is treated with 1. 2 NaOEt + 1,3-dibromopropane; 2. H3O+, heat?
questions.explanation: Treating Diethyl malonate with 1. 2 NaOEt + 1,3-dibromopropane; 2. H3O+, heat yields Cyclobutanecarboxylic acid. Rationale: Intramolecular dialkylation forms a cyclobutane diester, which undergoes decarboxylation to a cyclic acid.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1. NaOEt; 2. 1-Bromobutane; 3. Aqueous H3O+, heat to yield 2-Heptanone as the major product?
questions.explanation: Ethyl acetoacetate reacts with 1. NaOEt; 2. 1-Bromobutane; 3. Aqueous H3O+, heat to yield 2-Heptanone. Rationale: Enolate alkylation followed by beta-keto ester hydrolysis and spontaneous thermal decarboxylation.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Cyclohexanone is treated with 1. LDA; 2. PhSeCl; 3. H2O2?
questions.explanation: Treating Cyclohexanone with 1. LDA; 2. PhSeCl; 3. H2O2 yields 2-Cyclohexen-1-one. Rationale: Alpha-phenylselenide intermediate undergoes oxidative syn-elimination upon treatment with H2O2.
